title: Pulleys and conservation of work
subtitle: Trading distance pulled for lifting force

learn.prompt: A heavy 30 N crate sits 1 m from the fulcrum. Move the 10 N effort until the system balances.
learn.hint: Match the torques: 30 N x 1 m = 30 N m. Set effort distance = 30 N m / 10 N.
learn.explanation: 30 N x 1 m = 30 N m. For 10 N of effort, distance = 30 N m / 10 N = 3 m. The mechanical advantage is 3.

learn.prompt: A block-and-tackle system has 4 supporting ropes holding up a 400 N load. What effort force is needed to support the load?
learn.hint: The weight is distributed evenly across all supporting rope segments.
learn.explanation: With 4 supporting strands, each strand holds 400 N / 4 = 100 N of tension. The effort force required is 100 N.

misconceptionMap.b: That would be a single fixed pulley with no mechanical advantage.
misconceptionMap.c: Multiplying load by 4 calculates the wrong direction; pulleys reduce required effort.
misconceptionMap.d: A 2-rope system needs 200 N, but this system has 4 strands.

learn.prompt: You use a pulley system with an ideal mechanical advantage of 4 to lift a crate 0.5 m. How many meters of rope must you pull?
learn.hint: Ideal machines conserve work: distance pulled = IMA x distance lifted.
learn.explanation: Conservation of work means distance in = IMA x distance out = 4 x 0.5 m = 2.0 m.

learn.prompt: A hydraulic lift has a mechanical advantage of 15. What effort force in newtons is needed to lift a 3000 N car?

check.prompt: Does an ideal simple machine ever reduce the total work required to lift an object?
check.hint: Consider energy conservation: Work = Force x Distance.
check.explanation: No simple machine reduces work. Machines trade smaller input force for a proportionally greater input distance: Work in = Work out.

options.label: No — machines trade smaller force for greater distance, keeping work constant
Yes — machines create energy to make the load lighter
Yes — work is reduced by the mechanical advantage factor
No — machines always require twice as much work

misconceptionMap.b: Energy cannot be created; machines obey the law of conservation of energy.
misconceptionMap.c: Mechanical advantage reduces force, not energy or work.
misconceptionMap.d: Ideal machines lose no energy to friction.

check.prompt: A pulley system has an IMA of 3. To lift a 90 N box, set the required effort force in newtons.

takeaway.title: Machines trade force for distance
takeaway.body: Pulleys and levers amplify your force by distributing tension or extending lever arms. Work is conserved: reducing the force required requires pulling or moving proportionally farther.
